Fortify a graph for three-dimensional plotting

Source: R/layers-network.R
fortify.igraph.Rd

Turns an igraph graph into a node table with x, y and z positions. The edge table, with start and end positions taken from the node table, is attached to it and read by geom_edge_3d() through get_edges_3d(); ggplot(graph) therefore supports node and edge layers from one plot data set. Calling ggplot(graph, layout = ) passes the layout through to this method.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'igraph'
fortify(model, data = NULL, layout = NULL, dim = 3L, ...)

Arguments

model

An igraph graph (including tidygraph tbl_graph objects).

data

Unused, for compatibility with the generic.

layout

NULL, a numeric matrix with one row per vertex and two or three columns, or a layout function such as igraph::layout_with_kk().

dim

Number of layout dimensions requested from a layout function.

...

Unused.

Value

A data frame with one row per vertex: x, y, z, node (the vertex index), name and the vertex attributes. Its attribute "edges" holds one row per edge: from, to (vertex indices), x, y, z, xend, yend, zend and the edge attributes.

Details

The layout is computed by igraph, not by this package. With layout = NULL the vertex attributes x, y and z are used when the graph carries them (as for igraph::plot.igraph()), otherwise the three-dimensional Fruchterman-Reingold layout igraph::layout_with_fr() with dim = 3. A layout function is called with the graph, and with dim when it accepts it. A two-column layout places every node at z = 0.

References

Fruchterman and Reingold (1991). Graph drawing by force-directed placement. Software: Practice and Experience 21, 1129-1164. doi:10.1002/spe.4380211102

See also

geom_edge_3d(), stat_layers_3d()

Examples

if (requireNamespace("igraph", quietly = TRUE)) {
  set.seed(1)
  g <- igraph::sample_gnp(30, 0.1)
  nodes <- fortify(g, layout = igraph::layout_with_fr(g, dim = 3))
  head(nodes)
  head(get_edges_3d()(nodes))
}
